lore.ascendant.ascendant_protocol.title: The Ascendant Protocol
lore.ascendant.ascendant_protocol.summar: The emergency broadcast that turned survival into a framework.
lore.ascendant.ascendant_protocol.body: When the first rift opened over the Prime Meridian, ordinary people began to survive what should have killed them. The Ascendant Protocol was written as a field manual, not a prophecy: record every anomaly, test every limit, and never let a single hero become the only plan. Its authors disappeared before the second page was declassified.
lore.ascendant.prime_accord.title: The Prime Accord
lore.ascendant.prime_accord.summary: Six factions, one shared rule: power must remain accountable.
lore.ascendant.prime_accord.body: The Accord began as a ceasefire between rival programs that had been stealing the same anomalies. Its single enforceable clause is the origin ledger: every suit, power and archive entry must name the program that produced it. Signatories still argue over the rest, but no faction has dared to erase its own name.
lore.ascendant.kinetic_dynamics_brief.su: A speed program that measures success in control, not velocity.
lore.ascendant.kinetic_dynamics_brief.bo: Kinetic Dynamics built the Speedster Mk-I after a runner outran his own rescue team. The brief is blunt: acceleration without braking is a weapon pointed at the wearer. Every Mk-I ships with a kinetic dampener and a manual brake, and its pilots are trained to stop before they are trained to sprint.
lore.ascendant.forge_tech_ledger.title: Forge Tech Ledger
lore.ascendant.forge_tech_ledger.summary: The exosuit program that treats armor as a promise.
lore.ascendant.forge_tech_ledger.body: Forge Tech's ledger records every plate of the Titan Exosuit and the settlement it was forged to protect. The engineers refuse to sell a suit without a maintenance contract, and their field crews are known to abandon a contract when the buyer starts a war. Their motto is stamped inside the collar: a wall that walks away is still a wall.
lore.ascendant.abyssal_realm.title: The Abyssal Realm
lore.ascendant.abyssal_realm.summary: A drowned civilization that never stopped expanding.
lore.ascendant.abyssal_realm.body: The Abyssal Realm lies beneath a trench that appears on no reliable chart. Its regalia lets a surface dweller breathe, speak and fight in water, but the Realm expects something in return: a report on everything the wearer sees above the tide line. Its king has not surfaced in decades, and the trench keeps sending envoys anyway.
lore.ascendant.cosmic_vanguard.title: The Cosmic Vanguard
lore.ascendant.cosmic_vanguard.summary: Solar guardians who mistake endurance for permission.
lore.ascendant.cosmic_vanguard.body: The Cosmic Vanguard believes a star is a duty rather than a resource. Its Aegis suits can mend a wounded body and burn a threat from the sky, and its officers are taught to do both without asking which is more likely. The order's archive is open to anyone who survives a shift inside the solar observatory.
lore.ascendant.syndicate_shadow.title: The Syndicate's Shadow
lore.ascendant.syndicate_shadow.summary: An infiltration network that sells silence by the hour.
lore.ascendant.syndicate_shadow.body: The Syndicate does not sell weapons. It sells the moment before a weapon is noticed, which is why its Infiltrator suit hides a short-range teleport behind a civilian silhouette. Operatives are forbidden to leave a body they cannot explain, and the organization's real ledger is a list of clients who never learned each other's names.
lore.ascendant.null_wake.title: The Null Wake
lore.ascendant.null_wake.summary: A gravity anomaly that leaves evidence pointing inward.
lore.ascendant.null_wake.body: The Null Wake is not a creature. It is the footprint of something that fell through a gravity well and never finished landing. Observers near the impact site report crushed terrain arranged in rings, and every recovered fragment points toward a center that instruments cannot measure. The Forge Tech crew sent to survey it returned with a single instruction: do not dig.
lore.ascendant.first_flight.title: First Flight
lore.ascendant.first_flight.summary: The first recorded Ascendant flight ended in a controlled fall.
lore.ascendant.first_flight.body: The first flight trial lasted eleven seconds and covered forty meters before the pilot cut the thrust. The telemetry was unremarkable; the pilot's note was not. She wrote that the sky felt less like a destination and more like a surface that had been waiting for someone to stand on it.
lore.ascendant.kinetic_field_manual.summ: Why a speedster must practice stopping first.
lore.ascendant.kinetic_field_manual.body: Page one of the field manual is not about running. It describes how to release the field, how to bleed momentum into the ground, and how to fall without turning the fall into a projectile. Recruits who skip the chapter are assigned a partner whose only job is to time their stops.
lore.ascendant.trench_signal.title: Trench Signal
lore.ascendant.trench_signal.summary: A repeating pulse recorded during a propulsion test.
lore.ascendant.trench_signal.body: The signal was captured during a routine torrent propulsion test and has never been explained. It repeats every nineteen seconds, always from a different depth, and always stops when a diver tries to follow it. The Abyssal Realm's envoys refuse to translate the pattern, but they refuse to deny it exists.
lore.ascendant.solar_flare_log.title: Solar Flare Log
lore.ascendant.solar_flare_log.summary: A healer's account of the day the sun answered.
lore.ascendant.solar_flare_log.body: During a Vanguard exercise, a wounded cadet was pulled from a burning hangar and treated with a solar rejuvenation field. The medic's log records that the sun dimmed for exactly one heartbeat. The Vanguard calls it coincidence. The cadet, who now refuses to work indoors, calls it a receipt.
